claims_used.summary: Protein serving goal is 1.2 to 1.6 grams per kilogram of body weight per day, adjusted for individual calorie needs.

claims_used.summary: Saturated fat consumption should not exceed 10 percent of total daily calories.
One meal should contain no more than 10 grams of added sugars.
claims_used.source_locator: PDF page 5, Limit Highly Processed Foods, Added Sugars, and Refined Carbohydrates

claims_used.summary: The general population ages 14 and above should consume less than 2,300 milligrams of sodium per day.
For a 2,000 calorie pattern, the source gives serving goals for dairy, vegetables, fruits, and whole grains.
Dairy serving goal is 3 servings per day as part of a 2,000-calorie dietary pattern, adjusted for individual calorie needs.
Vegetable serving goal is 3 servings per day as part of a 2,000-calorie dietary pattern, adjusted for individual calorie needs.
claims_used.source_locator: PDF page 4, Eat Vegetables & Fruits Throughout the Day

claims_used.summary: Fruit serving goal is 2 servings per day as part of a 2,000-calorie dietary pattern, adjusted for individual calorie needs.
claims_used.source_locator: PDF page 4, Eat Vegetables & Fruits Throughout the Day

claims_used.summary: Whole grain serving goal is 2 to 4 servings per day, adjusted for individual calorie needs.
claims_used.source_locator: PDF page 4, Focus on Whole Grains

claims_used.summary: Grain snacks should not exceed 5 grams of added sugar per 3/4 ounce whole-grain equivalent.
claims_used.source_locator: PDF page 5, Limit Highly Processed Foods, Added Sugars, and Refined Carbohydrates

claims_used.summary: Dairy snacks should not exceed 2.5 grams of added sugar per 2/3 cup equivalent.

claims_used.summary: The major food allergens are milk, eggs, fish, Crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans, and sesame.
FDA has not established a threshold level for any allergens.
FoodSafety.gov frames home food safety around clean, separate, cook, and chill.
Perishable foods should be refrigerated within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when exposed to temperatures above 90 degrees F.
Hands should be scrubbed with soap and water for at least 20 seconds.
Food held hot after cooking should remain at 140 degrees F or above.
The temperature danger zone is between 40 degrees F and 140 degrees F.
Microwaved food should be cooked thoroughly to 165 degrees F or above.
Refrigerators should be set to 40 degrees F or below and freezers to 0 degrees F or below.
The DRI calculator uses height, weight, age, and activity level to generate estimated calorie needs and nutrient recommendations.
FoodData Central exposes REST endpoints for food search and food details and requires a data.gov API key.
